messages:
marie-sales: Heads-up — AtlasFin wants a 30-day POC next month. Requirements: VPC peering (GCP), IP allowlist, dedicated pool fallback if latency >150ms, SSO + SCIM, and answers to a security questionnaire. Can we sketch a quick provisioning runflow and who owns each step?

ben-eng: +1. I can own the dedicated pool config and gating rules. Quick runbook (high level):
1) Provision hosted API key for dev test (short-lived)
2) Prepare Dedicated pool template (GPU type + autoscale)
3) Create VPC peering + firewall allowlist
4) Entitlements: SSO, SCIM mapping, and KMS integration
5) QA + perf smoke tests, then handoff to Atlas for integration

alex-se: I can front the SSO/SCIM questions with the customer and gather metadata (IdP, SAML cert, admin emails). For hosted test, we usually create a scoped API key called `atlasfin-poc-2026` with rate limits and IP restrictions.

diego-infra: For the VPC peering (GCP) here's the minimal commands we use: 
```bash
gcloud compute networks peerings create redwood-atlasfin --network=redwood-vpc --peer-network=projects/atlasfin/global/networks/customer-vpc --peer-project=atlasfin --auto-create-routes
```
Also need a firewall rule to allow egress to our serving endpoint IP range (I can share the CIDR). Will need a ticket to whitelabel on their side.

sarah-sec: From security: we need answers for data at rest encryption, KMS key policy (customer-managed?), logging retention, SOC2/compliance evidence, and allowed personnel list for access. Send the customer a short checkbox form; I'll review. Also confirm whether they need private deployment (on-prem) or VPC-only.

marie-sales: Good — AtlasFin prefers VPC peering over on-prem for now. They asked about cost: do we have a standardized POC pricing (trial) for Dedicated?

ben-eng: We offer a discounted trial credit for Dedicated: typically 5000 USD in credits + hosted fallback enabled. If they want sustained load we can quote reserved commit. I'll pull the exact SKU and send pricing to you.

alex-se: Action items for this thread:
- marie-sales: collect IdP details and SCIM scope; ask Atlas to open a firewall ticket with their infra
- ben-eng: prepare Dedicated pool config + trial SKU; create sample `redwood.tf` snippet for them
- diego-infra: prepare peering CIDR and firewall text they can paste into ticket; open INF ticket on our side
- sarah-sec: draft security checkbox and list required docs

deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-972: "AtlasFin POC - VPC peering + firewall rules" assigned to diego-infra.

diego-infra: INF-972 details: need their network owner, peering project id, and the CIDR they want us to route. ETA for prepping our end: 48h after we get their answers.

marie-sales: Sharing first pass with Atlas now. One more question from them: can we pre-warm KV cache or provide sample throughput numbers for Dedicated qps per GPU?

ben-eng: For their expected seq len ~1024 and mixed prompts, rough numbers: ~120-200 req/s per A100x4 equivalent depending on batching. We can run a perf smoke test once pool is provisioned; will send sample load script.

alex-se: Link to public docs for SSO/KMS + runbook: https://redwood.example.com/docs/poc-setup (internal). I'll paste the form for IdP in a follow-up.

sarah-sec: I'll start the security form and tag in compliance for SOC2 docs. Please cc me on their answers.

marie-sales: Thanks — ping me when INF-972 moves or when you need me to nudge Atlas. :thumbsup:

ben-eng: I'll attach the Dedicated template and the short perf script to INF-972 by EOD.

alex-se: If we want a smooth demo, let's plan a canary traffic test day 3 of the POC. I'll add to the customer timeline.

marie-sales: Perfect. Closing thread for now — will re-open if Atlas pushes on timeline.
